vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: soul-in-sapphire
Version: 1.0.6

The skill is designed for legitimate AI agent self-reflection and memory management using Notion. However, it contains a path injection vulnerability in `scripts/ltm_common.js` and `scripts/notionctl_bridge.js` where the `NOTIONCTL_PATH` environment variable can override the path to the `notionctl.mjs` dependency. Although `fs.existsSync` is checked, an attacker controlling this environment variable and placing a malicious script at the specified path could achieve arbitrary code execution. While the `SKILL.md` contains prompt injection instructions for the AI agent to interpret shell commands and manage its identity, these instructions are aligned with the skill's benign self-improvement purpose and do not exhibit malicious intent like data exfiltration or unauthorized system modification.

llm.summary: The skill's code, declared requirements, and runtime instructions are coherent with a Notion-backed long-term memory and emotion/state journaling utility and do not request unexplained credentials or suspicious installs.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Notion LTM, emotion/state, journal, subagent payload prep) match the requests: node runtime, a NOTION_API_KEY, local config (~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json), and dependency on a local notion-api-automation helper. No unrelated credentials or binaries are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and scripts operate on the declared Notion DBs, read/write the local config file, and call a local notionctl (from the notion-api-automation skill) via child processes. This is in-scope for the stated purpose, but the skill does read/write local files (IDENTITY.md, ~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json) and will create/patch Notion databases during setup.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No remote downloads or package installers are included; this is instruction+script-only. All network access to Notion is performed through a local notionctl script (sibling skill). No URL-based installs or external binaries are fetched by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only NOTION_API_KEY (primary credential) and an optional NOTIONCTL_PATH are declared. These are appropriate: the skill must authenticate to Notion and may need an explicit path to notionctl. No unrelated secrets or excessive env variables are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false; the skill does not request permanent forced inclusion. It writes only its own config/state files and logs under its directories in the workspace and ~/.config, and does not modify other skills' configuration or system-wide agent settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is coherent for storing and recalling memories in Notion, but before installing: 1) Only supply a Notion integration token (NOTION_API_KEY) that you trust; review/restrict its permissions (database/page scopes) to least privilege. 2) Inspect the notion-api-automation/notionctl.mjs implementation (the skill invokes it via node) so you understand how your token is used. 3) Be aware the setup script will create Notion databases and write ~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json and some logs under the skill workspace (e.g., state/*.jsonl). If you want to limit blast radius, create a dedicated Notion Integration and workspace page for this skill rather than using a high-privilege token. 4) The skill depends on two other local skills (notion-api-automation and subagent-spawn-command-builder) — review those before enabling. Overall the package appears to do what it claims rather than contacting unexpected endpoints or asking for unrelated credentials.
